text:
Devon (customer): Hey @Anna — hitting a consistent 502 on Console -> Models when I click into a model detail. Happens ~30% of clicks. Banner shows request id: req_8f7a2c. Screenshot attached. Chrome 121 / macOS 14. Steps: login -> Console -> Models -> click model.

Anna (Support): Thanks — can you grab a network trace + console export for the same repro? That will let us see the failing request/response headers and any client errors. If possible include the request id, full request/response headers, and console errors.

Devon (customer): Okay — never done that before. Can you give steps for Chrome and Safari?

Anna (Support): Sure — quick checklist (Chrome/Edge):
1) Open DevTools: Cmd+Option+I (Mac) / Ctrl+Shift+I (Win).
2) Network tab -> check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
3) Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." to export console messages (or select and copy).
4) Reproduce the problem.
5) In Network tab -> right-click any row -> "Save all as HAR with content" (or top-right overflow menu -> Export HAR).
6) Name files like: devon_req_8f7a2c_console.log and devon_req_8f7a2c_network.har.

Notes: please keep the x-request-id header intact and DO NOT strip it. You may redact bearer tokens but leave header names and request/response status codes.

Sam (Eng): For a curl repro you can hit the same endpoint with the request id header to help us correlate traces. Replace placeholders below: 

```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/console/models/REPLACE_MODEL_ID' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACT_ME>' \
  -H 'x-request-id: req_8f7a2c' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
If the Console call is proxied, also record the browser request (the HAR) so we can see any frontend retries/redirects.

Lee (SRE): If you're on Firefox: open DevTools (F12) -> Network -> right-click -> "Save all as HAR". Or install the "HTTP Archive (HAR)" exporter add-on if older FF. For consoles: Console panel -> right-click -> "Save as...".

Anna (Support): Safari steps (Mac):
1) Enable Develop menu: Safari -> Settings -> Advanced -> "Show Develop menu in menu bar".
2) Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network tab.
3) Reproduce -> right-click network table -> "Export HAR" (or use the export icon).
4) Console: Console pane -> right-click -> "Save as...".

Devon (customer): Got it. Any extras you want?

Sam (Eng): A few extras help a lot:
- Full repro steps (click sequence, account used, any feature flags).
- Time window of failure (approx minute).
- Any local proxies / VPNs.
- Whether you were logged in as an org admin or member.

Anna (Support): Once you have the files, upload here: https://files.redwood.com/debug/upload — set visibility to internal and include metadata in the filename: thread-1977777777_devon_req_8f7a2c.zip. If the upload UI asks, tag with: support, console, 502.

Devon (customer): Uploaded the HAR + console logs (filename thread-1977777777_devon_req_8f7a2c.zip). Link: https://files.redwood.com/d/abc123 (shared).

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2027-022 for request id req_8f7a2c — assigned to Sam and Lee. :rotating_light:

Lee (SRE): Thanks — I pulled the bundle. Early look shows a backend 502 with upstream timeout around 2026-03-17T15:12:10Z plus a client-side retry. Sam, can you grep logs for req_8f7a2c across the proxy and runtime?

Sam (Eng): On it. If we need a customer-facing summary I'll draft one after we confirm root cause.

Anna (Support): Thanks Devon — will follow up here once we have a root cause and ETA for a fix. If you see the issue again, please keep the session open and add another HAR so we can compare. :thumbsup:
